claim: Let \(x\) be an Abelian pattern Sturmian word. After possibly interchanging its two letters, write \(x=\mathbf 1_D\) with \(D=\{d_0<d_1<\cdots\}\subset\mathbb N_0\). Then for every integer \(N\ge 0\), \[\sum_{\substack{d\in D\\ d\le N}}(d+1)\le 2N+1,\] hence \(d_n\ge 2^n-1\) for every \(n\ge 0\) and \[|D\cap[0,N]|\le 1+\lfloor\log_2(N+1)\rfloor.\] These bounds are sharp simultaneously: \(D_*=\{2^n-1:n\ge0\}\) has a forest incidence graph and therefore \(\mathbf 1_{D_*}\) is Abelian pattern Sturmian, with \(d_n=2^n-1\) for every \(n\), \(|D_*\cap[0,N]|=1+\lfloor\log_2(N+1)\rfloor\) for every \(N\), and equality in the weighted prefix inequality whenever \(N=d_n\).
integrity: The proof is self-contained after two explicitly cited inputs from arXiv:2609.28059v1: the incidence-forest characterization and the sufficient gap criterion used to certify the sharp example. No numerical experiment or external certification is used to prove the infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is confined to the binary Abelian pattern Sturmian class characterized by a forest sum-incidence graph. It is not a density theorem for arbitrary Sidon sets and does not address the higher-alphabet extremal questions in the source paper.
title: Sharp logarithmic support envelope for Abelian pattern Sturmian words
